subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 20, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 20, 2026

Good morning from Spokane! The team has been busy squashing bugs and hardening our infrastructure this week, and we're excited to share what's new. Our latest development cycle focused heavily on resolving update conflicts that affected some installed systems. The geocode-glib fix is now live and should make your next system update much smoother.

On the installer front, Darren pushed several Calamares improvements that will benefit both new and returning users. We've added better support for older Nvidia graphics cards and switched the default boot resolution to 1080p instead of native 4K, which should prevent display issues on a wider range of hardware. Disk encryption has been removed from the default install path, giving users the flexibility to configure it post-install if they choose.

Security has been top of mind across the broader Arch ecosystem this week. The AUR malware incident that compromised over 400 packages serves as a stark reminder of why repository sovereignty matters — something we've prioritized since day one. Arch's decision to pause new AUR registrations was the right call, and we're monitoring the situation closely as maintainers work to restore trust.

Our own infrastructure got a security upgrade too. Natalie configured secret detection and static analysis scanning in our GitLab CI pipelines, adding automated guardrails that catch potential issues before they reach production. The us-infra-hub project also gained a new MCP stdio server, expanding our internal tooling capabilities for infrastructure management.

In community news, the Discord server has been lively with discussions about the recent Arch developer resignation after a decade of contributions. It's a significant moment for the ecosystem, and many of our users have shared thoughtful perspectives on what sustainable open-source maintenance looks like. We're grateful for the civil, constructive conversations happening in our channels.

The CachyOS feature on How-To Geek sparked some great dialogue about Arch accessibility. It's validating to see the "Arch without the installation nightmare" narrative gaining traction — that's exactly what we've been building with AcreetionOS. Several newcomers mentioned discovering us through that article, and we welcome you all.

For this week's tip: if you're running an older Nvidia card and experienced boot issues previously, grab the latest ISO and give it another try. The 1080p gfxmode default and improved driver detection should get you to a working desktop without manual intervention. As always, the wiki has step-by-step guides for post-install encryption setup.

We also want to highlight the Systemtap 5.6 release that landed in upstream repositories. This powerful tracing toolkit is invaluable for debugging kernel-level issues, and having the latest version available means our users can leverage improved probe support and performance enhancements. Check the Arch wiki for practical examples.

That's a wrap for today's update! Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community — whether you're running our ISO, contributing code, or just following along. We'll be back tomorrow with more. Stay safe, stay sovereign, and happy computing.
